The use of the drug, epirubicin, as adjuvant chemotherapy for breast cancer is associated with an increased risk of heart failure and death.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a predictive model of the effects of a single dose of an anthracycline on the outcome of patients with breast cancer, and the validation of this model in an independent dataset.
the use of anthracyclines in the adjuvant treatment of breast cancer.
the development of new, more accurate methods for predicting the benefit of adjuvant anthracycline chemotherapy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is no evidence that anthracycline chemotherapy is beneficial in women with breast cancer.
the evidence for the efficacy of epirubicin in the treatment of breast cancer is strong.
there is no conclusive evidence that anthracycline-based regimens are superior to CMF-based regimens in terms of overall survival.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have demonstrated that a number of factors can be used to predict the benefit of anthracyclines in early breast cancer.
we have identified a number of potential predictive markers for anthracycline treatment in breast cancer.
we have shown that a 21-gene assay can provide information on risk of distant metastatic recurrence, which is independent of the traditional clinical-pathological factors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we can use the same model to predict the benefit of anthracyclines in different breast cancer populations, and that this is a useful tool to help clinicians make treatment decisions.
